CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ankle injury from basketball

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Jerry is a 45-year-old male who presents with a right ankle injury sustained today while playing basketball with his son. Patient reports going up for a shot when his son made contact with him during defense. Patient landed awkwardly and twisted his ankle. He describes pain on the outside of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. Patient reports difficulty walking and describes the ankle as not feeling stable or solid. Patient notes he recently returned to a consistent gym workout routine and is concerned about disruption to his fitness regimen. Patient also mentions he has volunteered to coach basketball starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports lateral ankle pain, swelling, bruising, and instability. Denies other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not documented

MEDICATIONS
Meloxicam prescribed today

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Son Sean, age 10, plays basketball

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. Recently returned to regular gym workouts. Plays basketball recreationally with his son. Will be coaching basketball starting in April. Has dogs at home.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Ankle: Swelling noted on lateral side. Exquisite tenderness over lateral malleolus. Mild tenderness over medial deltoid region. Skin intact without epidermolysis. Brisk capillary refill noted. No significant malalignment. Patient able to stand on ankle but reports pain and instability with weight-bearing.

RESULTS
X-ray of right ankle (AP, lateral, and oblique views): Displaced lateral malleolus fracture at Weber C level. No evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Lateral malleolar fracture, right ankle, displaced, Weber C level with associated instability. Surgical intervention recommended with placement of plate and screws. Patient to remain non-weight bearing with crutches. Conservative measures: Ice and elevation of ankle. Patient works from home and able to elevate regularly. Meloxicam prescribed for pain and swelling. Expected recovery time approximately 3 months. Patient encouraged to continue coaching duties as planned starting in April. Gradual return to exercise and athletic activity anticipated within 3-month recovery window.
